rich_text.plain_text: Vilhelm Hammershøi: Silence

text.content: Vilhelm Hammershøi: Silence

rich_text.plain_text: (Hauser & Wirth Publishers, 2024). A slim recent way in to the quietest painter in the North: 106 pages built around eighteen works, all from private collections and some barely exhibited before, with essays by Felix Krämer and Florian Illies. Don't go to it for a full career survey. Go to it for the grey Copenhagen rooms, the closed doors, the figure turned away at the window.

rich_text.plain_text: Harald Sohlberg: Painting Norway

text.content: Harald Sohlberg: Painting Norway

rich_text.plain_text: (Dulwich Picture Gallery, 2019). The catalogue from Sohlberg's first major UK exhibition, made with the National Museum in Oslo and built around Winter Night in the Mountains, the painting at the top of this page, which won NRK's 1995 public vote for Norway's national painting. Out of print, so hunt it down secondhand. Worth the effort.

rich_text.plain_text: Nikolai Astrup: Visions of Norway

text.content: Nikolai Astrup: Visions of Norway

rich_text.plain_text: (Yale University Press, 2021). Edited by MaryAnne Stevens, with a prelude by Karl Ove Knausgård. Astrup painted western Norway as somewhere half real and half remembered: midsummer bonfires, marsh marigold meadows, the garden he planted himself. Colour that still looks radical a century on.

rich_text.plain_text: Harriet Backer: Every Atom is Colour

text.content: Harriet Backer: Every Atom is Colour

rich_text.plain_text: (Hirmer, 2023). The catalogue of the retrospective that travelled from Oslo to Stockholm, Paris and Bergen. Backer painted interiors like Hammershøi did, but where he drains the colour away she pours it in, lamplight and blue shadow and all. Long overdue, and beautifully made.

rich_text.plain_text: Hilma af Klint: Paintings for the Future

text.content: Hilma af Klint: Paintings for the Future

rich_text.plain_text: (Guggenheim, 2018). The book of the New York show that became the most visited in the Guggenheim's history. Af Klint was painting vast, radiant abstractions years before Kandinsky, then asked for them to be kept from view for twenty years after her death. If abstraction is your way in, this is the one.

rich_text.plain_text: If you're only buying one, make it the Munch. Prideaux's biography is the book that changes how you read everything else here, because it puts a life behind the pictures instead of more pictures. If it's colour and reproduction you're after, Astrup and Backer give you far more to look at for the money. And if the Hammershøi is what tempts you, know what you're getting: a beautiful exhibition book, not a career.
